findings.evidence: Mark interactive elements with labels such as `[Submit]`, `[ ] checkbox`, `(v) dropdown`.
findings.fix: Cut the generic wireframe notation (buttons, checkboxes, dropdowns): the model already uses these conventions. Keep only the non-obvious ones (scroll edge marks, modal as an inner box over the base screen).

findings.evidence: 6. **Ask which to pick**, numbered. If the user rejects all, ask which ranked task each option got wrong, then redraw.
findings.fix: Steps 5-6 are generic present-and-ask steps. Replace them with a domain decision, for example: before you ask, state which mockup you recommend for the top-ranked task and why. Then the step carries expert judgment.

findings.evidence: use Unicode box-drawing only if the user asks (common for TUIs), then check border alignment in a monospace font. Display width differs across fonts, which shifts borders.
findings.fix: Replace the check the agent cannot run (it cannot view a font) with a concrete gotcha: East Asian ambiguous-width and emoji characters take 2 columns in many terminals. Keep box-drawing lines free of such characters, and count wide characters as 2 when checking row lengths.

Make the example match its title and step 5. Either draw a sidebar next to the table or rename the example to 'Aligned table'. Also show the four rationale points as four bullets (Approach, Favors, Drawback, Best fit) instead of the single line '- Approach / Favors / Drawback / Best fit'.

findings.evidence: Default to 3 structurally distinct mockups ... compare records -> aligned table vs cards ... Navigation placement (top, side, none) is the fallback axis.
findings.fix: Each task branch gives only 2 variants. Say where the third comes from, for example: 'When the dominant-task axis yields only two variants, take the third from the navigation-placement axis.'
